### Provide environment information

```

  Browsers:
    Chrome: 112.0.5615.137
    Safari: 16.3
```

```
"@trpc/server": "10.23.0",
```

### Describe the bug

routers don't seem to check the types of their procedures or sub-routers. self contained example:

```ts
import {initTRPC} from '@trpc/server'
import {createNextApiHandler} from '@trpc/server/adapters/next'

const trpca = initTRPC.context<{a: string}>().create()
const trpcb = initTRPC.context<{b: string}>().create()

const parent = trpca.router({
  a: trpca.procedure.query(({ctx}) => ctx.a.slice()),
  b: trpcb.procedure.query(({ctx}) => ctx.b.slice()),
})

export default createNextApiHandler({
  router: parent,
  createContext: () => ({a: 'aaa'}),
})
```

this is fine at compile time, and hitting `/api/trpc.a` works, but hitting `/api/trpc.b` gets `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'slice')` (since `ctx.b` is never defined anywhere) - I shouldn't have been allowed to use `trpcb.procedure.query(...)` on a router for `trpca`, since they have different contexts.

### Link to reproduction

https://www.typescriptlang.org/play?ts=5.0.3#code/JYWwDg9gTgLgBAb2AO2DAKgJQAoGEC+cAZlBCHAOQACMUYAxgPQDOAplAG7sUBQoksRPSisAhjFYA5VgA8YAQTDAAEqOQATADbtCJMpRp0mbTu0aj1osBKjNGyWTF496EZM3i0GouAF44KGhYeAB0rsgScgA8CKIAXHAeUCgA5vgAfAAUAJRhIuKsOS5uHnBe9ABGfgGoGDi4YW6RMDEVCUmpGTl5YhJFxe7wYKIiEdXloiGkAK42mQg8cHDxZUaTYKT0rOrTIiEAjtPsAJ6Z8-QwMvjZfulwFzIhk8yawFs52QA0i3BtqwwVEIbCBbHZ7Q4nM4IB7XW73S4hQEvN6FbJfHjXHg8WQCeDqVhEUTTTTwYS9KSORQqNRadjzH4zGwJYajGDfJZkgq4JqOBI5OHzFYUUQiijXb7XIA

### To reproduce

Paste the code above into a next api handler. I tried that above using the stackblitz suggested but there's a strange compile error that I don't get locally, it doesn't seem to acknowledge that the export for the next adapter exists: https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-qwqz1i-qs9elv?file=src/pages/api/trpc/[trpc].ts

### Additional information

My use-case: I'm trying to make a router in a library, which can be plugged into an application's parent router for modular functionality, with the requirement that the parent has a context which meets the requirement of the library router. But the type system doesn't seem to enforce this. Maybe it's just not supported (yet)?

I'm putting yes I'd be down to fix this but I don't know if I'll have the time to so if someone else wants to, go for it!

items.title: feat: Support typesafe inputs in `t.middleware` created middlewares
Experimental: a simpler backend API for FormData loading, and foundation for loading other data types

labels.name: ❄️  icebox
labels.description: features / PRs that might be pick up in the future and can be handy to keep track of

items.body:
Supersedes #4286 

Goals:

* Add a simpler API for standing up FormData loading middleware and inputs
* Remove the need for req to be provided by the user's ctx
* Lay groundwork for future data types support and cross-adapter data loading middlewares

This piece will have the effect of supporting FormData in _all_ our adapters, and making it easy for community Adapters to participate in the data loading middlewares we build, as well as write their own middlewares, adapters, and content-handlers to support complete protocols

Implemented stuff:

* New `RequestUtils` type which an Adapter can optionally pass to wrap its Request type up in a decoupled interface. If not passed but a middleware tries to use it, there will be a runtime error blaming the Adapter
* RequestUtils passed all the way through to middlewares meaning they can read off the request without needing knowledge of the adapter(s) they live within (and without further user setup of ctx)
* The middleware APIs have been wrapped up into a middleware factory `experimental_createFormDataMiddleware` which has some sensible defaults, and on construction will return a middleware - I will be later proposing formal factory patterns which we'll document for library authors, and this is an example of the core pattern I'd like us to promote
* `TRPCInstance` and `AnyTRPCInstance` - initTRPC has been a bit of a complex type to unwrap, these bring it in line with many of our other APIs in permitting abuse of the type for generics and factories. First internal usage is in `experimental_createFormDataMiddleware`

items.title: Add experimental procedure extensions API
items.body:
Closes #4191 

#4191 requests a way for a middleware to extend a baseProcedure with some required input data

ALSO we would _love_ to make it easier for 3rd party vendors such as authentication, authorisation, logging, crashlytics, analytics, etc, tools to provide 1-line integrations without knowing _anything about the contents of `t`_ (which is currently impossible

ALSO we would love for monorepo owners to be able to write middlewares in a completely `t` agnostic way, for the same reasons of separation as 3rd parties _need_ that agnostic behaviour to write anything

This PR adds `createProcedureExtension` which can be used to create an extension function, receiving the ProcedureBuilder as an input and being permitted to make whatever changes it likes. Some early thoughts:

* This is a powerful API and may be subject to misuse and anti-patterns, but also opens a whole new world of 3rd party integrations up to us
* This API exposes many builder methods which we have no proven use case for currently, should we Pick<T> the methods we actually want to expose? How would that work with the builder API?
* What happens if an input is an array and the extension wants to add an object to it? (and vice versa)
* What about meta? Should be enable the extending of the meta type from a chained `.meta` call? Might open some additional doors here but isn't currently a feature of tRPC although both input and context can do it.

items.title: feat: Polymorphic tRPC routes in react client
items.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

When defining routers which have common interfaces, it can be helpful to also define common UI which just needs to be informed about the particular route it will be using. For instance:

```tsx
// Route structure like: { foo: { create, update, list, delete }, bar: { create, update, list, delete } }
const trpc = createTRPCReact 

type CrudRoute = typeof trpc.bar

function MyComponent({ route }: { route: CrudRoute }) {
  const createMutation = route.create.useMutation()
  const listQuery = route.delete.useQuery({ /* paging params */ })

  return /* ui */
}

function MyScreen() {
  // We then pass a route which matches the interface but isn't the one the type was derived from
  // Error because the query key does not match!
  return <MyComponent route={trpc.foo} />
}
```

Currently for even the most basic example, this doesn't work because `DecoratedProcedureRecord` calculates `TPath` based on the full path to a procedure name and down the type chain into react query's `TQueryKey` on `QueryObserverOptions`. TPath/TQueryKey is important type information of course.

It would be helpful to have some type utilities provided which can extract the abstract type information from a Route/Procedure and produce a type which can be used for polymorphism. The design of this I'm not too sure as fairly complex cases might exist where parameter/return types may vary slightly but have some common underlying interface.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see

A proof of concept for the simple use case (where the underlying interface of the procedures is identical) looks like this:

```tsx
import { AnyProcedure, AnyRouter, ProcedureRouterRecord } from '@trpc/server'
import {
  DecoratedProcedureRecord,
  DecorateProcedure,
} from '@trpc/react-query/dist/shared'

type AbstractDecoratedProcedureRecord<
  TProcedures extends ProcedureRouterRecord,
  TFlags
> = {
  [TKey in keyof TProcedures]: TProcedures[TKey] extends AnyRouter
    ? AbstractDecoratedProcedureRecord<
        TProcedures[TKey]['_def']['record'],
        TFlags
      >
    : TProcedures[TKey] extends AnyProcedure
    ? DecorateProcedure<TProcedures[TKey], TFlags, any>
    : never
}

/**
 * Given a tRPC react route, calculates the abstract type so that similar interfaces can be passed polymorphically
 *
 * Ie. For: `trpc.routeA.routeB = { procA, procB }`
 * Usage: `AbstractProcedureRecord<typeof trpc.routeA.routeB>`
 */
export type AbstractProcedureRecord<
  T extends DecoratedProcedureRecord<any, any, any>
> = T extends DecoratedProcedureRecord<infer TProcedures, infer TFlags, any>
  ? AbstractDecoratedProcedureRecord<TProcedures, TFlags>
  : never

//
// Usage
//

import { trpc } from './react-client/api'

export type RouteDef = BaseProcedureRecord<
  typeof trpc.foo
>

// Now any matching interface can be assigned polymorphically
const r1: RouteDef = trpc.foo
const r2: RouteDef = trpc.bar
```

### Describe alternate solutions

There is a lot more to this, the above solution may not work where routes don't have the exact same interface. The full solution might involve taking the recursive union of an arbitrary number of route types which could get hairy

```
type AbstractProcedureRecord<T1, T2, T3, ...TEtc> = /* calculate the common abstract type */
```

Or less hackily, maybe a way to actually define an interface which a Router must implement on the API side, and then provide an API to use these interfaces alongside the React Client library

### Additional information

_No response_

### 👨‍👧‍👦 Contributing

- [x] 🙋‍♂️ Yes, I'd be down to file a PR implementing this feature!

items.title: New link architecture
items.body:
> **Breaking change** for next major! Full WIP of ideas for next major in #887 

## New link architecture

- Heavily inspired by RxJS
- Each link needs to return an observable which is responsible for subscribing to `next()` observable - https://www-git-katt-observable-new-trpc.vercel.app/docs/links#creating-a-custom-link
- The data in the links also receive "Error responses" from the backend - they aren't considered "errors" by the links themselves, that's up to the interpretation of the `TRPCClient`
- The data in the links are now wrapped in response object `{ context, data }` to links that can add metadata (like the original `Response`) to
- Data transformers are moved to being a link - https://www-git-katt-observable-new-trpc.vercel.app/docs/data-transformers#3-add-to-createtrpcclient-or-setupnext-config
- Add new `setupTRPC()` method to `packages/next` to simplify setup - https://www-git-katt-observable-new-trpc.vercel.app/docs/nextjs#3-create-trpc-hooks

### What it (hopefully) enables

- Should enable us to write a `@trpc/react-lite`-package that doesn't depend on `react-query` where each feature is composable by a link. **This is not the goal in itself**, but it's good that the architecture now (should) allow it.
- Enable better integration with other frameworks that might not have stuff like `react-query`
- More power for people using `@trpc/client`
- Ability to access response metadata (#1353)

### Open questions

- Should the `next()`-call in a link maybe be called `forward()` instead to not to confuse with observables' next concept?
- Should we just use RxJS instead of having our own implementation?
- Should response errors be errors in the chain? Could be a `TRPCResponseError` - might work easier with things like retry

### Notes from @KATT

- I'm quite new to observables/RxJS, so keen to get feedback on people who've used it more


### Q&A

> This is a **fat** PR - where can I look to get a feel of it?

- https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/katt/observable-new/packages/client/src/links/dedupeLink.ts
- https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/katt/observable-new/packages/client/src/links/retryLink.ts

> OK, cool, where's the core juice at that I can review?

- https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/katt/observable-new/packages/client/src/rx
- https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/katt/observable-new/packages/client/src/links/internals/createChain.ts

> Why is it not [ES Observable](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-observable)-compliant?

- I hate `this` in JS and try to avoid it all cost.
- _If_ we think this a good idea further on, backwards compatibility should be achievable be added by mapping `observable` to `new Observable()`-factory fn

> Why not use RxJS/x?

- I don't want tRPC to have dependencies
- RxJS is quite heavy
- RxJS doesn't allow me to specify a generic for `Error`s

> Fuck me, this is a lot, I can't possibly review this

Happy to organize a community call / 1on1 Zoom call for anyone interested in helping out.
